questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend demoing the rejection path and a stopping condition firing, not just the happy path, when presenting the capstone?
options: The happy path cannot technically be demonstrated

An interviewer who builds agents has seen plenty of happy-path demos; showing what happens when something is denied, limited, or logged demonstrates the skill this course actually spent six chapters building
Rejections and stopping conditions are required by the Claude API to be shown in every demo
The happy path is not part of the capstone project at all
questions.explain: The lesson argues that failure-path handling — rejections, stopping conditions, logging — is the differentiated, harder-to-fake skill worth showing, since most candidates only demo success.

Five different tools with no logging or limits

questions.explain: The portfolio sentence explicitly lists the approval checkpoint, append-only logging, iteration/cost limits, and least-privilege credentials as the verified controls built across the capstone.

The checkpoint, rejection handling, and escalation design applied to issue_refund
